examples.en: The cup fell on the floor and broke.

examples.ko: 창문이 깨어져서 방 안으로 바람이 들어와요.
examples.en: The window is broken, so wind comes into the room.

examples.ko: 약속이 깨어지면 서로 마음이 많이 아파요.
examples.en: When a promise is broken, both people get hurt.
I carried the plate carefully in case it broke.
The moment the dream was shattered, I felt so empty.

examples.ko: 두 사람의 사이가 깨어지지 않았으면 좋겠어요.
examples.en: I hope the relationship between the two of them doesn't break.

explain: '깨지다'와 같은 뜻이고, 말할 때는 줄여서 '깨져요, 깨졌어요'라고 많이 해요. 컵이나 유리 같은 물건뿐 아니라 약속, 꿈, 분위기, 사이가 무너질 때도 써요. 잠에서 '깨다'와는 다른 말이니 헷갈리지 마세요.
explain_en: It means the same as '깨지다', and in speech people often shorten it to '깨져요' or '깨졌어요'. It is used for objects like cups and glass, and also for promises, dreams, moods and relationships falling apart. Don't confuse it with '깨다' (to wake up from sleep).

examples.en: Read the passage above and answer the following questions.
I answered the teacher's question right away.

examples.ko: 그는 속내를 드러내기 싫어서 질문에 답하지 않았어요.
examples.en: He didn't want to reveal his feelings, so he didn't answer the question.
It takes a while to reply to the email.

examples.ko: 어떻게 답할지 몰라서 잠깐 가만히 있었어요.
examples.en: I didn't know how to answer, so I stayed quiet for a moment.

examples.ko: 면접에서 질문에 침착하게 답하는 연습을 했어요.
examples.en: I practiced answering questions calmly in an interview.

explain: '대답하다'와 거의 같지만, '답하다'는 시험 문제, 설문, 글처럼 글로 된 질문에 많이 나와요. 짝말은 '묻다'이고, 편지나 메시지에 답할 때는 '답장하다'도 써요. 사람에게 말할 때는 '~에게 답하다', 질문에는 '~에 답하다'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is almost the same as '대답하다', but '답하다' often appears with written questions such as test items, surveys and texts. Its counterpart is '묻다', and for letters or messages you can also say '답장하다'. Use '~에게 답하다' for a person and '~에 답하다' for a question.

examples.en: When I turned on the light, the room quickly became bright.
The eastern sky began to get lighter little by little.

examples.ko: 새 전구로 바꿨더니 거실이 훨씬 밝아져요.
examples.en: Since I changed the bulb, the living room is much brighter.

examples.ko: 날씨가 좋아지면서 마음도 밝아지는 것 같아요.
examples.en: As the weather gets better, my mood seems to brighten too.
I edited the photo and the face looks brighter and prettier.

examples.ko: 해가 뜨면 하늘이 점점 밝아질 거예요.
examples.en: When the sun rises, the sky will gradually get brighter.

explain: 빛뿐 아니라 표정, 분위기, 성격이 환해질 때도 써요. 반대말은 '어두워지다'예요. '밝다'는 상태이고 '밝아지다'는 변하는 과정이라서, 예전보다 나아졌다고 말할 때 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: It is used not only for light but also when an expression, mood or personality becomes cheerful. The opposite is '어두워지다'. '밝다' describes a state while '밝아지다' describes the change, so it fits when something has become better than before.

examples.ko: 동생은 화가 나면 말끝이 짧아지고 목소리가 높아져요.
examples.en: When my younger sibling is angry, their sentences get clipped and their voice gets higher.
When winter comes, the days gradually get shorter.
I got a haircut and my hair got a lot shorter.
I washed the pants and it seems the length got shorter.

examples.ko: 방학이 짧아지면 여행 계획도 바꿔야 해요.
examples.en: If the vacation gets shorter, we have to change our travel plans too.

examples.ko: 시간이 부족해서 회의가 짧아질 것 같아요.
examples.en: We're short on time, so the meeting will probably be shorter.

explain: 반대말은 '길어지다'예요. 길이뿐 아니라 시간, 말, 글이 줄어들 때도 써요. '줄어들다'는 양이나 수가 적어질 때 더 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: The opposite is '길어지다'. It is used for length, but also when time, speech or writing gets shorter. '줄어들다' fits better when an amount or number decreases.

examples.ko: 아무리 화가 나도 사람들 앞에서 욕하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: No matter how angry you are, you shouldn't swear in front of people.

examples.ko: 친구가 뒤에서 나를 욕했다는 말을 들었어요.
examples.en: I heard that my friend badmouthed me behind my back.

examples.ko: 운전 중에 화가 나서 혼자 욕했어요.
examples.en: I got angry while driving and swore to myself.

examples.ko: 아이가 욕하는 걸 보고 깜짝 놀랐어요.
examples.en: I was shocked to see the child cursing.

examples.ko: 남을 욕하지 말고 먼저 내 잘못을 생각해 봐요.
examples.en: Don't badmouth others; think about your own mistakes first.

examples.ko: 다들 그 감독을 욕했지만 영화는 인기가 많았어요.
examples.en: Everyone criticized the director, but the movie was very popular.

explain: 거친 말을 하는 것과, 누군가를 심하게 나쁘게 말하는 것 둘 다에 써요. 사람에게는 '~을/를 욕하다'라고 하고, '욕을 하다'처럼 띄어 써도 돼요. '목욕하다'와 글자가 비슷하지만 전혀 다른 말이에요.
explain_en: It covers both using rough language and harshly speaking ill of someone. With a person, say '~을/를 욕하다', and you can also split it as '욕을 하다'. It looks similar to '목욕하다' (to bathe) but is a completely different word.

examples.ko: 새 집에 놓을 소파를 가구점에서 샀어요.
examples.en: I bought a sofa for my new home at a furniture store.

examples.ko: 가구점에 가면 침대와 책상을 한꺼번에 볼 수 있어요.
examples.en: At a furniture store, you can see beds and desks all at once.

examples.ko: 우리 동네 가구점도 일요일에 문을 열어요.
examples.en: The furniture store in my neighborhood is open on Sundays too.

examples.ko: 이사하기 전에 가구점 몇 군데를 돌아다녔어요.
examples.en: Before moving, I went around a few furniture stores.

examples.ko: 집 근처에 큰 가구점이 새로 생겼어요.
examples.en: A big furniture store opened near my house.

examples.ko: 그 가구점은 가격이 싸고 배달도 해 줘요.
examples.en: That furniture store has low prices and also delivers.

explain: '서점', '꽃집'처럼 가게 이름에 '-점'이나 '-집'을 붙이는 말 중 하나예요. 일상에서는 '가구 가게'라고도 해요. 가구를 사러 갈 때는 '가구점에 가다'라고 말해요.
explain_en: It is one of the shop names formed with '-점' or '-집', like '서점' and '꽃집'. In daily talk people also say '가구 가게'. When you go to buy furniture, you say '가구점에 가다'.

examples.ko: 어느 맑은 가을날에 가족과 함께 산에 갔어요.
examples.en: On a clear autumn day, I went to the mountains with my family.
The afternoon sunlight of an autumn day is so warm.

examples.ko: 오늘처럼 시원한 가을날이면 밖에 나가고 싶어요.
examples.en: On a cool autumn day like today, I want to go outside.

examples.ko: 가을날엔 낙엽 밟는 소리가 정말 좋아요.
examples.en: On autumn days, I really like the sound of stepping on fallen leaves.

examples.ko: 비 오는 가을날은 왠지 마음이 쓸쓸해요.
examples.en: A rainy autumn day somehow makes me feel lonely.
I kept the autumn day I spent with friends in photos.

explain: '가을철'이 가을이라는 기간을 말한다면 '가을날'은 가을의 어느 하루와 그날의 분위기를 말해요. 같은 식으로 '봄날, 여름날, 겨울날'도 써요. '어느 가을날'처럼 이야기를 시작할 때 자주 어울려요.
explain_en: While '가을철' refers to the autumn period, '가을날' refers to a single autumn day and its atmosphere. In the same way you can say '봄날, 여름날, 겨울날'. It works well for starting a story, as in '어느 가을날' (one autumn day).

examples.en: The autumn breeze is blowing, so it's perfect for a walk.
I walked slowly along the river in the autumn breeze.
Leaves fall one by one in the autumn wind.
The autumn breeze is cool, but it gets a bit cold in the evening.
I opened the window and heard the sound of the autumn wind.
I listened to a song as refreshing as an autumn breeze.

explain: 선선하고 시원한 느낌이 먼저 떠올라서 '가을바람이 불다', '선선한 가을바람'처럼 자주 써요. 차갑게 세게 부는 '찬바람'과는 느낌이 달라요. 노래나 글에서는 쓸쓸한 마음을 말할 때도 나와요.
explain_en: It first brings to mind a cool, pleasant feeling, so it is often used as '가을바람이 불다' or '선선한 가을바람'. It feels different from '찬바람' (cold wind), which is harsher. In songs and writing it can also express a lonely mood.

examples.ko: 조용한 가을밤에는 귀뚜라미 소리가 크게 들려요.
examples.en: On a quiet autumn night, you can hear crickets loudly.
As the autumn night deepens, it gets colder and colder.
I spent the cool autumn night talking with a friend.

examples.ko: 가을밤엔 따뜻한 차 한 잔이 생각나요.
examples.en: On autumn nights, I think of a cup of warm tea.
An autumn night with a bright moon is good for a walk.
Please play music as quiet as an autumn night.

explain: 서늘하고 차분한 분위기가 먼저 떠올라서 달, 벌레 소리, 산책 같은 말과 잘 어울려요. 같은 식으로 '여름밤, 겨울밤'도 써요. 가을의 하루를 말하는 '가을날'과 짝으로 기억하면 좋아요.
explain_en: It brings to mind a cool, calm atmosphere, so it goes well with words like moon, insect sounds and walks. You can say '여름밤' and '겨울밤' in the same way. It is handy to remember it as a pair with '가을날', which refers to an autumn day.

examples.ko: 가을철에는 일교차가 커서 감기에 걸리기 쉬워요.
examples.en: In autumn the temperature gap between day and night is big, so it's easy to catch a cold.
When autumn comes, the leaves change color on every mountain.

examples.ko: 가을철 별미로 밤과 고구마를 많이 먹어요.
examples.en: People eat a lot of chestnuts and sweet potatoes as autumn treats.
Autumn has nice weather, so it's good for traveling.

examples.ko: 가을철엔 낮과 밤의 온도 차이가 커요.
examples.en: In autumn, the temperature difference between day and night is large.
With autumn here, the number of hikers has jumped.

explain: '철'은 어떤 계절이나 시기를 말해서, '가을철'은 가을이라는 기간을 가리켜요. 하루를 말하는 '가을날'과 달리 건강이나 안전을 알리는 뉴스와 안내문에 자주 나와요. '봄철, 여름철, 겨울철'도 같은 식으로 써요.
explain_en: '철' refers to a season or period, so '가을철' points to the autumn period as a whole. Unlike '가을날', which means one day, it often appears in news and notices about health or safety. '봄철, 여름철, 겨울철' work the same way.

examples.en: We decided to hold a family meeting this weekend.

examples.ko: 우리는 가족회의에서 여름 여행 장소를 정했어요.
examples.en: We chose our summer trip destination at a family meeting.
The family meeting starts after dinner.
A family meeting was suddenly called, so I felt a bit nervous.

examples.ko: 가족회의 때 모두 자기 의견을 말해요.
examples.en: At family meetings, everyone says their own opinion.
In our house, we decide big matters through a family meeting.

explain: '가족회의를 열다/하다'처럼 말해요. 회사의 딱딱한 회의와 달리 집에서 편하게 의견을 나누는 자리라는 느낌이에요. 이사, 여행, 용돈처럼 가족이 함께 정할 일에 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: You say it as '가족회의를 열다/하다'. Unlike a stiff business meeting, it feels like a relaxed time at home to share opinions. It suits things a family decides together, such as moving, trips or allowances.

examples.en: I prepared fruit as a snack for the kids.

examples.ko: 소풍 갈 때 간식거리를 넉넉히 챙겼어요.
examples.en: I packed plenty of snacks for the picnic.

examples.ko: 냉장고를 열어 봤는데 간식거리가 하나도 없어요.
examples.en: I opened the fridge, but there are no snacks at all.

examples.ko: 시험공부할 때 먹을 간식거리 좀 사 올게요.
examples.en: I'll go buy some snacks to eat while studying for the exam.

examples.ko: 간식거리는 너무 달지 않은 게 좋아요.
examples.en: Snacks are better when they're not too sweet.

examples.ko: 간식거리에 돈을 너무 많이 쓰는 것 같아요.
examples.en: I think I spend too much money on snacks.

explain: '간식'이 먹는 것이나 그 시간을 두루 말한다면, '간식거리'는 간식으로 먹을 만한 재료나 음식을 말해요. '먹을거리, 볼거리'처럼 '-거리'가 붙어 '그럴 만한 것'을 나타내요. 집에 간식이 있는지 없는지 말할 때 잘 쓰여요.
explain_en: While '간식' broadly means snacks or snack time, '간식거리' refers to the foods you have on hand to snack on. Like '먹을거리' and '볼거리', the '-거리' ending gives the sense of 'something worth doing or having'. It is handy when talking about whether there are snacks at home.

examples.en: I give the puppy its food every morning.

examples.ko: 개밥이 다 떨어져서 사료를 사러 가요.
examples.en: We ran out of dog food, so I'm going to buy some.

examples.ko: 개밥 그릇이 비어 있어서 물도 새로 담았어요.
examples.en: The dog's bowl was empty, so I also filled it with fresh water.

examples.ko: 우리 개는 개밥보다 간식을 더 좋아해요.
examples.en: My dog likes treats more than its regular food.

examples.ko: 개밥은 사람 음식과 달리 간을 하지 않아요.
examples.en: Unlike human food, dog food isn't seasoned.

examples.ko: 바빠서 아침에 개밥도 못 주고 나왔어요.
examples.en: I was busy and left in the morning without even feeding the dog.

explain: 개에게 주는 밥이고, 사료나 개 먹이와 비슷하게 써요. 보통 '개밥을 주다'라고 말해요. 속담 '개밥에 도토리'에도 나와서 함께 알아 두면 좋아요.

phrases.example: 새 학교에서 친구가 없어서 개밥에 도토리가 된 기분이었어요.
phrases.en: At the new school I had no friends, so I felt like the odd one out.
phrases.nuance_ko: 무리에 끼지 못하고 따로 노는 사람을 말해요. 조금 쓸쓸하거나 놀리는 느낌으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a person who can't fit in with a group and stays apart. It carries a slightly lonely or teasing tone.

explain_en: It is the food given to a dog, used much like 'dog food' or 'dog feed'. People usually say '개밥을 주다'. It also appears in the proverb '개밥에 도토리', which is worth learning together.

examples.en: If you come across the bridge, my house is right there.
The kid from next door came over to our house.
I ran into a friend while crossing the road to this side.

examples.ko: 강 건너편 마을에서 배를 타고 건너와요.
examples.en: People cross over by boat from the village on the other side of the river.
A letter that came across the sea arrived today.
Come over to this side and sit together.

explain: '건너다'는 방향이 없지만 '건너오다'는 말하는 사람 쪽으로 넘어올 때 써요. 반대로 저쪽으로 갈 때는 '건너가다'라고 해요. 길, 다리, 강, 바다처럼 사이에 있는 것을 지나 올 때 자연스러워요.
explain_en: '건너다' has no direction, but '건너오다' is used when someone crosses toward the speaker's side. When going the other way, you say '건너가다'. It sounds natural for passing over something in between, like a road, bridge, river or sea.

examples.ko: 우리 강아지가 큰 천둥소리에 겁먹고 침대 밑에 숨었어요.
examples.en: Our puppy got scared by the loud thunder and hid under the bed.
Don't be scared, it doesn't hurt at all.

examples.ko: 처음 비행기를 탔을 때 많이 겁먹었어요.
examples.en: I was really scared the first time I rode an airplane.

examples.ko: 뭘 그렇게 겁먹어요? 아무 일도 아니에요.
examples.en: What are you so scared of? It's nothing.
He looked at the teacher with a frightened face.

examples.ko: 겁먹을 필요 없어요. 면접은 금방 끝나요.
examples.en: There's no need to be scared. The interview ends quickly.

explain: '무서워하다'와 비슷하지만 '겁먹다'는 두려움이 마음에 들어와 움츠러든 모습을 말해요. '겁먹지 마'처럼 격려하는 말로 자주 나와요. '겁이 나다'는 두려운 마음이 저절로 생기는 느낌이고, '겁을 먹다'처럼 띄어 써도 돼요.
explain_en: It is similar to '무서워하다', but '겁먹다' shows someone shrinking back because fear has taken hold. It often appears in encouraging phrases like '겁먹지 마'. '겁이 나다' means fear arises on its own, and you can also split this word as '겁을 먹다'.

examples.en: It was a winter day when snow was falling heavily.
On cold winter days, I crave something with warm broth.
The sunshine on a winter day is brief but warm.

examples.ko: 어느 겨울날 할머니가 털장갑을 떠 주셨어요.
examples.en: One winter day, my grandmother knitted me wool gloves.

examples.ko: 겨울날엔 일찍 해가 져서 금방 어두워져요.
examples.en: On winter days, the sun sets early and it gets dark quickly.

examples.ko: 바람이 센 겨울날이면 집에서 영화를 봐요.
examples.en: On windy winter days, I watch movies at home.

explain: 겨울의 어느 하루와 그날의 분위기를 말해요. 겨울이라는 기간을 말하는 '겨울철'과 달리 이야기나 추억에 자주 어울려요. '가을날, 봄날, 여름날'과 같은 식으로 써요.
explain_en: It refers to one day in winter and the mood of that day. Unlike '겨울철', which means the winter period, it often fits stories and memories. It works like '가을날', '봄날' and '여름날'.

examples.en: Winter rain is falling, so the roads are very slippery.
I walked home in the cold winter rain.

examples.ko: 겨울비는 눈보다 더 춥게 느껴질 때가 있어요.
examples.en: Winter rain sometimes feels colder than snow.

examples.ko: 겨울비에 옷이 다 젖어서 감기에 걸렸어요.
examples.en: My clothes got soaked in the winter rain and I caught a cold.
Today's hike was canceled because of the winter rain.
Even winter rain is fine when it comes after such a long time.

explain: 겨울인데 눈이 아니라 비가 올 때 써요. 눈이 올 줄 알았는데 비가 오면 '눈 대신 겨울비가 오네요'처럼 말할 수 있어요. 차갑고 쓸쓸한 느낌으로 글이나 노래에도 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is used when rain falls in winter instead of snow. If you expected snow but got rain, you can say '눈 대신 겨울비가 오네요'. It also often appears in writing and songs with a cold, lonely feeling.

examples.ko: 두꺼운 겨울옷은 옷장 맨 위 칸에 있어요.
examples.en: The thick winter clothes are on the top shelf of the closet.

examples.ko: 지금 겨울옷을 세일해서 값이 많이 싸요.
examples.en: Winter clothes are on sale now, so the prices are low.
My winter clothes have gotten too small, so I have to buy new ones.

examples.ko: 여행 갈 때는 겨울옷도 꼭 챙기세요.
examples.en: Be sure to pack winter clothes too when you travel.
I haven't put away my winter clothes yet.
I dressed my child in a thick jacket as winter wear.

explain: 반대말은 '여름옷'이에요. 계절이 바뀔 때 '겨울옷 정리', '겨울옷을 꺼내다'처럼 자주 말해요. '겨울 옷'처럼 띄어 쓰지 않고 한 낱말로 써요.
explain_en: The opposite is '여름옷'. When the seasons change, people often say '겨울옷 정리' or '겨울옷을 꺼내다'. It is written as one word, '겨울옷', without a space.

examples.en: I put the wedding ring on my left ring finger.

examples.ko: 결혼반지는 두 사람의 약속을 보여 주는 상징이에요.
examples.en: A wedding ring is a symbol of the promise between two people.
My wedding ring has gotten too small and is hard to take off.
We chose the same design for our wedding rings.
We decided to go order the wedding rings together too.
We engraved both of our names on the wedding rings.

explain: 반지는 '끼다'라고 하고, 빼는 것은 '빼다'예요. 연인끼리 맞추는 반지는 '커플링'이라고 따로 불러요. 결혼할 때 맞추는 반지라서 '결혼반지를 맞추다'라는 말도 자주 써요.
explain_en: For rings, you use '끼다' to wear and '빼다' to take off. A ring a couple orders as a pair is called '커플링', which is a separate word. Since people have them made when they marry, '결혼반지를 맞추다' (to order wedding rings) is also a common phrase.

examples.en: A wedding photo is hanging on the living room wall.
We went to a studio to take wedding photos.
Mom was really pretty in her wedding photo.

examples.ko: 결혼사진은 결혼식 전에 미리 찍기도 해요.
examples.en: Wedding photos are sometimes taken in advance, before the ceremony.
Is our whole family in the wedding photo?

examples.ko: 새로 찍은 결혼사진으로 휴대폰 배경을 바꿨어요.
examples.en: I changed my phone wallpaper to our newly taken wedding photo.

explain: 결혼식 날 찍은 사진과 스튜디오에서 따로 찍은 사진 둘 다 가리킬 수 있어요. 일상에서는 '웨딩 사진'이라고도 해요. '결혼사진을 찍다', '결혼사진을 보다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It can refer both to photos taken on the wedding day and to photos taken separately at a studio. In daily talk people also say '웨딩 사진'. You use it like '결혼사진을 찍다' or '결혼사진을 보다'.

examples.en: I packed rolled omelet as a side dish for my lunchbox.

examples.ko: 계란말이는 불을 약하게 해서 천천히 말아야 해요.
examples.en: For rolled omelet, you should keep the heat low and roll it slowly.

examples.ko: 계란말이에 파와 당근을 넣으면 더 맛있어요.
examples.en: Rolled omelet is tastier with green onion and carrot in it.

examples.ko: 엄마가 만들어 주신 계란말이가 제일 맛있어요.
examples.en: The rolled omelet my mom makes is the tastiest.
At the restaurant, I ordered one more rolled omelet too.

examples.ko: 아이들은 계란말이만 있어도 밥을 잘 먹어요.
examples.en: Kids eat their rice well as long as there's rolled omelet.

explain: '달걀말이'라고도 하며 둘 다 맞는 말이에요. 도시락 반찬이나 식당 밑반찬으로 자주 나와요. 풀어 놓은 달걀을 얇게 부어 돌돌 말아서 만들어요.
explain_en: It is also called '달걀말이', and both forms are correct. It often shows up as a side dish in lunchboxes and at restaurants. It is made by pouring thin layers of beaten egg and rolling them up.

examples.ko: 추운 날에는 따뜻한 고깃국이 먹고 싶어요.
examples.en: On cold days, I want to eat warm meat soup.
My grandmother put rice into the meat soup for me.
The longer you boil meat soup, the richer the broth gets.
Tonight's meal is meat soup and kimchi.

examples.ko: 고깃국을 끓일 때 무를 같이 넣어요.
examples.en: When I make meat soup, I put in radish too.

examples.ko: 고깃국 한 그릇이면 밥 한 공기가 뚝딱이에요.
examples.en: With one bowl of meat soup, a bowl of rice disappears in no time.

explain: 고기를 넣고 끓인 국을 두루 말하는 이름이에요. 실제 식당에서는 '곰탕', '소고기뭇국'처럼 더 구체적인 이름을 써요. 집에서 '고깃국 끓였어'처럼 편하게 말할 때 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: It is a general name for soup boiled with meat. At restaurants people use more specific names like '곰탕' or '소고기뭇국'. It fits casual home talk such as '고깃국 끓였어' (I made meat soup).

examples.en: We chose a BBQ restaurant for the company dinner.
After work, I met my friends at a BBQ restaurant.

examples.ko: 우리 동네 고깃집은 항상 손님이 많아요.
examples.en: The BBQ restaurant in my neighborhood always has lots of customers.

examples.ko: 고깃집에 가면 상추와 마늘도 같이 나와요.
examples.en: At a BBQ restaurant, lettuce and garlic come out with the meat.
I heard the meat at this BBQ restaurant is tender and tasty.
I booked a BBQ restaurant for a family meal out.

explain: 불판에 고기를 직접 구워 먹는 식당을 말할 때 많이 써요. '삼겹살집', '갈빗집'처럼 메뉴 이름에 '집'을 붙이기도 해요. 회식이나 가족 외식 장소로 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is commonly used for restaurants where you grill meat yourself at the table. People also attach '집' to menu names, as in '삼겹살집' and '갈빗집'. It often comes up as a place for company dinners and family outings.

examples.ko: 고모부가 추석에 맛있는 과일을 보내 주셨어요.
examples.en: My uncle sent delicious fruit for Chuseok.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 고모부와 낚시를 자주 갔어요.
examples.en: When I was little, I often went fishing with my uncle.
My uncle's health has gotten much better lately.
On New Year's Day, I bowed to my uncle.
My uncle runs a small shop in Seoul.

examples.ko: 고모부의 차를 타고 할머니 댁에 갔어요.
examples.en: We went to Grandma's house in my uncle's car.

explain: 아버지 쪽 고모의 남편이에요. 어머니 쪽 이모의 남편은 '이모부'라고 따로 불러요. 높여 말할 때는 '고모부께서는, 고모부께'처럼 써요.
explain_en: This is the husband of your father's sister. The husband of your mother's sister is called '이모부', a separate word. To show respect, use forms like '고모부께서는' and '고모부께'.

examples.en: We played dodgeball at the playground with a small rubber ball.

examples.ko: 고무공은 땅에 떨어지면 높이 튀어 올라요.
examples.en: A rubber ball bounces high when it hits the ground.
The puppy ran over with the rubber ball in its mouth.
The rubber ball flew over the fence.
I got hit by a rubber ball, but it didn't hurt as much as I thought.
I bought a rubber ball at the mart too.

explain: 고무로 만든 공이라서 통통 튀는 느낌이 있어요. '축구공, 농구공'처럼 경기 이름이 붙은 공과 달리 놀이용 공을 말할 때 잘 어울려요. '고무공이 통통 튀다'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: Because it is made of rubber, it has a bouncy feel. Unlike balls named after a sport, such as '축구공' and '농구공', it fits a play ball. You say things like '고무공이 통통 튀다' (the rubber ball bounces).

examples.en: On holidays, I go down to my hometown house to see my family.

examples.ko: 고향집은 산 아래에 있는 작은 마을이에요.
examples.en: My hometown house is in a small village at the foot of a mountain.
After a long time, I started missing my hometown house.
At my hometown house, my mother prepared a meal for me.

examples.ko: 방학이 되면 기차를 타고 고향집으로 돌아가요.
examples.en: When vacation comes, I take the train back to my hometown house.
There was a persimmon tree in the yard of my hometown house.

explain: '고향'이 지역을 말한다면 '고향집'은 내가 자랐거나 부모님이 사시는 집을 말해요. 결혼한 사람이 부모님 집을 말할 때는 '본가'라고도 해요. '고향집에 내려가다'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: While '고향' refers to a region, '고향집' refers to the house where you grew up or where your parents live. A married person may also call their parents' house '본가'. You say '고향집에 내려가다' (to go down to the hometown house).

examples.en: I had warm gomtang for lunch.
Gomtang is made by boiling beef bones for a long time.

examples.ko: 곰탕에 소금과 파를 넣어 간을 맞춰요.
examples.en: You season gomtang by adding salt and green onion.
This restaurant is really famous for its gomtang.
One bowl of gomtang here, please.
Gomtang and kkakdugi go really well together.

explain: 소고기와 뼈를 오래 끓인 뽀얗고 맑은 국이에요. 식당에서는 보통 깍두기와 함께 나와요. '설렁탕'과 비슷한 음식으로 같이 파는 식당도 많아요.
explain_en: It is a clear, milky soup made by boiling beef and bones for a long time. At restaurants it usually comes with kkakdugi (radish kimchi). It is similar to '설렁탕', and many restaurants sell both.

examples.ko: 계산기로 삼 곱하기 삼을 해 보면 구가 나와요.
examples.en: If you do three times three on a calculator, you get nine.
Do you know what six times four is?
Multiplication is a little harder to calculate than addition.
We learned multiplication in math class today.
Multiplication and division are opposite calculations.

examples.ko: 이 문제는 먼저 곱하기부터 해야 해요.
examples.en: For this problem, you have to do the multiplication first.

explain: '삼 곱하기 삼은 구'처럼 한자어 숫자(일, 이, 삼…)로 읽어요. 짝말은 '더하기, 빼기, 나누기'예요. 동사는 '곱하다'이고, 구구단을 외울 때도 이 말이 나와요.
explain_en: You read it with Sino-Korean numbers (일, 이, 삼…), as in '삼 곱하기 삼은 구'. Its companions are '더하기, 빼기, 나누기'. The verb is '곱하다', and the word also comes up when memorizing the times tables.

examples.en: There is a public restroom in the park, which is convenient.

examples.ko: 공중화장실은 모두가 같이 쓰는 곳이라 깨끗하게 이용해야 해요.
examples.en: A public restroom is shared by everyone, so you should keep it clean.
I walked for a long time looking for a public restroom on the street.
Where is a public restroom near here?
Sometimes there is no toilet paper in a public restroom.
I ran in a hurry to the public restroom at the subway station.

explain: 공원, 지하철역, 길가처럼 누구나 쓰는 화장실이에요. 말할 때는 그냥 '화장실 어디예요?'라고 해도 돼요. '공중화장실'은 안내판이나 뉴스처럼 구분해서 말할 때 더 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is a restroom anyone can use, like those in parks, subway stations and streets. In speech you can simply ask '화장실 어디예요?'. '공중화장실' shows up more on signs and in news, where it needs to be distinguished.

examples.en: Airport buses have plenty of room for luggage.

examples.ko: 공항버스를 타면 공항까지 한 시간쯤 걸려요.
examples.en: If you take the airport bus, it takes about an hour to the airport.

examples.ko: 공항버스 정류장이 호텔 바로 앞에 있어요.
examples.en: The airport bus stop is right in front of the hotel.
It's an early-morning flight, so we decided to go by airport bus.
Please check the airport bus timetable in advance.
I have a lot of luggage, so the airport bus is more convenient than the subway.

explain: 짐을 실을 공간이 있어서 공항에 갈 때 많이 타요. '공항 리무진'이라고도 불러요. 일반 시내버스와 달리 공항 노선을 따로 운행해요.
explain_en: It has space for luggage, so many people take it to the airport. It is also called '공항 리무진'. Unlike an ordinary city bus, it runs on its own airport routes.

examples.en: I peeled the apple thinly with a fruit knife.

examples.ko: 과일칼은 손잡이를 꼭 잡고 써야 해요.
examples.en: You have to hold the handle firmly when using a fruit knife.
Please take a fruit knife out of the drawer.
The fruit knife got dull, so I bought a new one.
It's dangerous for a child to use a fruit knife alone.
I packed a fruit knife too when going camping.

explain: 작고 날이 짧은 칼이고 '과도'라고도 많이 불러요. 사과나 배 껍질을 깎을 때 써요. '칼을 쓰다', '껍질을 깎다'와 같이 말해요.
explain_en: It is a small knife with a short blade, and it is also often called '과도'. You use it to peel apples or pears. It pairs with phrases like '칼을 쓰다' and '껍질을 깎다'.

examples.en: I borrowed an interesting science book from the library.
The science book has many pictures, so it's easy to understand.
My younger sibling likes reading science books.
The science book was more fun than I expected, which surprised me.
The science books are in the children's section of the bookstore.

examples.ko: 이번 달에는 과학책도 몇 권 샀어요.
examples.en: This month I bought a few science books too.

explain: '소설책, 동화책, 만화책'처럼 내용에 따라 책 종류를 말할 때 써요. 어린이가 읽는 과학 이야기 책을 떠올릴 때 특히 자연스러워요. 책을 세는 말은 '권'이에요.
explain_en: It is used like '소설책', '동화책' and '만화책' to name a type of book by its content. It sounds especially natural for science storybooks that children read. The counter for books is '권'.

examples.en: I went on a group trip by tour bus.

examples.ko: 관광버스는 출발 시간을 꼭 지켜야 해요.
examples.en: For a tour bus, you must keep to the departure time.
The tour bus arrived at the mountain entrance.
We shared snacks on the tour bus.
Traveling by tour bus is easy even if you don't know the way.
People boarded the tour bus one after another.

explain: 여행객이 단체로 타고 관광지를 다니는 버스예요. 시내버스나 시외버스와 달리 여러 명이 빌려 타는 경우가 많아요. 학교 소풍이나 단체 여행 이야기에 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is a bus that groups of travelers ride to visit tourist spots. Unlike city or intercity buses, it is often rented by a group. It frequently comes up in stories about school outings and group trips.

examples.en: This video was made for children's education.
My child learns Hangul with an educational app.
This game is educational, not for entertainment.
This book is for teaching, so the pictures are easy.
There are ones for education and ones for play.
It's material too good to be used only for teaching.

explain: '-용'은 쓰임새를 나타내서 '가정용, 업무용, 연습용, 어린이용'처럼 써요. '교육용 자료', '교육용 프로그램'처럼 뒤의 명사를 꾸미는 말로 많이 나와요. 반대로 즐기려는 것은 '오락용'이라고 해요.
explain_en: The suffix '-용' shows purpose, as in '가정용, 업무용, 연습용, 어린이용'. It often modifies a following noun, as in '교육용 자료' or '교육용 프로그램'. For things meant for fun, you say '오락용'.

examples.en: A traffic police officer is directing cars at the intersection.
I asked a traffic police officer for directions.

examples.ko: 교통경찰은 신호등이 고장 나면 수신호로 차를 안내해요.
examples.en: When a traffic light is broken, traffic police direct cars with hand signals.
My childhood dream was to be a traffic police officer.
The car stopped when it saw the traffic officer's hand signal.

examples.ko: 눈이 오는 날에는 교통경찰도 바빠 보여요.
examples.en: On snowy days, even the traffic police look busy.

explain: 도로에서 차와 사람의 흐름을 안내하고 단속하는 경찰이에요. 일상에서 직접 부를 때는 그냥 '경찰관'이라고도 해요. 짝말로 '수신호', '교통정리'가 자주 나와요.
explain_en: This is the police officer who guides and monitors the flow of cars and people on the road. When addressing one directly, you can also just say '경찰관'. Common companions are '수신호' (hand signals) and '교통정리' (traffic control).

examples.en: My shoelace came undone, so I tied it again.

examples.ko: 구두끈을 너무 꽉 묶으면 발이 아파요.
examples.en: If you tie your shoelaces too tight, your feet hurt.

examples.ko: 새 구두끈으로 바꾸니 구두가 달라 보여요.
examples.en: With new laces, the dress shoes look different.
I almost tripped on my shoelace while running.
You have to make a strong knot in your shoelaces.
The length of the laces differs by shoe too.

explain: 구두에 달린 끈이에요. 운동화까지 포함해서 말할 때는 '신발끈'이 더 넓게 쓰여요. '끈을 묶다, 끈이 풀리다'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: This is the lace on dress shoes. When you mean laces on any shoes including sneakers, '신발끈' has a wider range. You say things like '끈을 묶다' (tie the lace) and '끈이 풀리다' (the lace comes undone).

examples.en: I ordered fried dumplings at the Chinese restaurant.
Fried dumplings taste best when they are cooked crispy.
I dip fried dumplings in soy sauce.
The kids only ate the fried dumplings and left the jjajangmyeon.

examples.ko: 여기 군만두 한 접시 더 주세요.
examples.en: One more plate of fried dumplings here, please.

examples.ko: 집에서 만든 군만두가 가게 것보다 맛있어요.
examples.en: Homemade fried dumplings taste better than the ones from the shop.

explain: 기름에 구워 겉이 바삭한 만두예요. 쪄서 먹는 '찐만두', 삶아서 먹는 '물만두'와 비교해서 알아 두면 좋아요. 중국집에서 '군만두 하나 주세요'라고 자주 주문해요.
explain_en: These are dumplings pan-fried in oil until the outside is crispy. It helps to compare them with '찐만두' (steamed) and '물만두' (boiled). At Chinese restaurants people often order with '군만두 하나 주세요'.

examples.en: I got earrings as a birthday present.
My earring fell off and I searched for it for a long time.
There is a small gem set in the earrings.
The right earring is missing.
I bought both the earrings and the necklace as a set.

examples.ko: 이 귀고리는 가벼워서 오래 해도 편해요.
examples.en: These earrings are light, so they're comfortable even after a long time.

explain: '귀걸이'라고도 하며 일상에서 두 말을 다 써요. 동사는 '귀고리를 하다', '귀고리를 끼다/달다'처럼 말하고, 한 쪽은 '한 짝'이라고 세요. 귀에 하는 장식이니 '목걸이, 팔찌'와 짝으로 외우면 좋아요.
explain_en: It is also called '귀걸이', and both words are used in daily life. You say '귀고리를 하다' or '귀고리를 끼다/달다', and one earring is counted as '한 짝'. It helps to learn it together with '목걸이' and '팔찌'.

examples.en: In elementary school, I wrote a picture diary every day.
I drew what happened today in my picture diary.

examples.ko: 그림일기는 글솜씨가 없어도 쓸 수 있어서 좋아요.
examples.en: A picture diary is nice because you can write one even without good writing skills.
An old picture diary turned up in the drawer.
Writing a picture diary is one of the vacation homework assignments.
I looked back on the day with my child through a picture diary.

explain: 초등학교 저학년 때 방학 숙제나 수업으로 많이 쓰는 일기예요. 어른이 되어 '그림일기를 쓰다'라고 하면 그림으로 하루를 기록한다는 느낌이에요. '일기를 쓰다'와 같이 동사는 '쓰다'를 써요.
explain_en: This is the kind of diary many children write in lower elementary grades as vacation homework or class work. When an adult says '그림일기를 쓰다', it feels like recording the day with drawings. As with '일기를 쓰다', the verb is '쓰다'.

examples.ko: 커피를 사 오는 그사이에 비가 그쳤어요.
examples.en: The rain stopped in the meantime while I went to buy coffee.
It's been a while. You've really changed a lot in the meantime.

examples.ko: 바쁜 그사이에도 가족 생각을 놓지 않았어요.
examples.en: Even in that busy time, I never stopped thinking of my family.

examples.ko: 회의가 시작되기 전 그사이를 이용해 숙제를 끝냈어요.
examples.en: I used the time before the meeting started to finish my homework.
There was not a single contact in the meantime.

examples.ko: 일이 끝나고 저녁 먹기 전 그사이가 제일 편해요.
examples.en: The gap between finishing work and eating dinner is the most relaxing.

explain: '그동안'은 쭉 이어진 기간을 말하고, '그사이'는 두 일 사이의 틈을 가리켜요. 그래서 '잠깐 자리를 비운 그사이'처럼 짧은 틈에 일어난 일을 말할 때 잘 어울려요. '그 사이'처럼 띄어 쓰기도 해요.
explain_en: '그동안' refers to a continuous period, while '그사이' points to the gap between two events. So it suits things that happen in a short gap, as in '잠깐 자리를 비운 그사이' (while I stepped away for a moment). You will also see it written as '그 사이'.

examples.ko: 월급이 매달 하순에 들어와서 그전에는 돈이 빠듯해요.
examples.en: My pay comes in late each month, so money is tight before that.

examples.ko: 그전 같으면 이런 일에 화를 냈을 거예요.
examples.en: In the past, I would have gotten angry about something like this.

examples.ko: 그전과 비교하면 요즘은 훨씬 여유가 있어요.
examples.en: Compared to before, I have much more breathing room these days.
I sometimes think of the neighborhood where I lived before.
I have changed a lot from who I was before.

examples.ko: 그전엔 매일 걸어서 출근했는데 지금은 차로 가요.
examples.en: I used to walk to work every day, but now I go by car.

explain: '예전'이 막연히 오래전을 가리킨다면 '그전'은 앞에서 말한 일이나 때보다 앞선 시간을 가리켜요. '그전에는, 그전 같으면'처럼 지금과 비교할 때 자주 나와요. '그 전'처럼 띄어 쓰기도 해요.
explain_en: While '예전' vaguely points to long ago, '그전' points to a time before the event or time just mentioned. It often appears when comparing with now, as in '그전에는' and '그전 같으면'. You will also see it written as '그 전'.

examples.en: I won a prize at a writing contest.

examples.ko: 글짓기를 좋아하는 친구와 같은 모둠이 됐어요.
examples.en: I got put in the same group as a friend who likes writing.
Writing gets easier the more you read.
I'm worried because I'm not confident in writing.
Writing was hard at first, but now it's fun.
I envy the friend who won a prize for writing.

explain: 시, 동화, 일기처럼 글을 지어 쓰는 활동을 말해서, 학교의 '글짓기 대회, 글짓기 시간'에 많이 나와요. '글쓰기'는 보고서나 메일까지 두루 쓰는 말이고 '글짓기'는 창작하는 느낌이 더 있어요. 동사는 '글을 짓다' 또는 '글짓기를 하다'라고 해요.
explain_en: It refers to composing texts like poems, stories or diaries, and appears often in school contexts such as '글짓기 대회' and '글짓기 시간'. '글쓰기' is broader and covers even reports and emails, while '글짓기' has more of a creative feel. The verb forms are '글을 짓다' or '글짓기를 하다'.

examples.ko: 첫돌 때 받은 금반지를 지금도 서랍에 보관하고 있어요.
examples.en: I still keep the gold ring I received on my first birthday in a drawer.
The price of a gold ring changes depending on the price of gold.
The gold ring is too small and won't go on my finger.

examples.ko: 결혼 선물로 금반지 한 쌍을 샀어요.
examples.en: I bought a pair of gold rings as a wedding gift.
I asked them to engrave a name on the gold ring.
Both a gold ring and a silver ring suit you well.

explain: 금으로 만든 반지예요. 한국에서는 아기의 첫돌에 선물하는 금반지를 '돌반지'라고 따로 불러요. 짝말로 '은반지'가 있고, 동사는 '끼다'를 써요.
explain_en: It is a ring made of gold. In Korea, the gold ring given as a gift on a baby's first birthday has its own name, '돌반지'. Its counterpart is '은반지' (silver ring), and the verb is '끼다' (to wear).

examples.en: I took a commemorative photo with my friends at the graduation ceremony.

examples.ko: 기념사진은 가족 모두 모여서 찍기로 했어요.
examples.en: We decided to take the commemorative photo with the whole family together.

examples.ko: 여행지마다 기념사진이 한 장씩 남아 있어요.
examples.en: There is one commemorative photo left from each travel spot.

examples.ko: 기념사진 속 우리는 모두 활짝 웃고 있어요.
examples.en: In the commemorative photo, we are all smiling broadly.
I printed it as a commemorative photo and put it in a frame.

examples.ko: 죄송하지만 기념사진 한 장만 찍어 주시겠어요?
examples.en: Excuse me, could you take one commemorative photo for us?

explain: 졸업식, 여행, 생일처럼 기억에 남기고 싶은 날에 찍는 사진이에요. 보통 '기념사진을 찍다'라고 하고, 조금 격식 있게는 '기념 촬영'이라고도 해요. 여럿이 함께 찍으면 '단체 기념사진'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It is a photo taken on a day you want to remember, such as a graduation, trip or birthday. You usually say '기념사진을 찍다', and a bit more formally '기념 촬영'. A photo taken with many people is called '단체 기념사진'.

examples.en: It's chilly in the morning and evening, so I wear long sleeves.
I want to buy a long-sleeved shirt.

examples.ko: 더운 날에도 일할 때는 긴소매가 편해요.
examples.en: Even on hot days, long sleeves are comfortable for working.

examples.ko: 반소매 말고 긴소매로 바꿔 입고 와요.
examples.en: Change into long sleeves instead of short sleeves and come back.

examples.ko: 이 옷은 긴소매인데도 얇아서 안 더워요.
examples.en: Even though this top has long sleeves, it's thin, so it isn't hot.
Long sleeves are a bit hot to wear in summer.

explain: 반대말은 '반소매'예요. 일상 대화에서는 '긴팔, 반팔'이라고 더 편하게 말하는 사람도 많아요. '긴소매 옷, 긴소매 셔츠'처럼 옷 이름 앞에 붙여 써요.
explain_en: The opposite is '반소매'. In everyday talk, many people casually say '긴팔' and '반팔' instead. It is placed before a clothing name, as in '긴소매 옷' and '긴소매 셔츠'.

examples.en: The side of the road in front of my house is all flower beds.
I bought an umbrella at a shop beside the road.

examples.ko: 길옆으로 자전거 도로가 길게 나 있어요.
examples.en: A bike path runs long along the side of the road.

examples.ko: 급한 전화가 와서 차를 길옆에 잠깐 세웠어요.
examples.en: An urgent call came, so I briefly parked the car by the roadside.
Yellow leaves are falling from the trees along the road.
Streetlights stand in a row beside the road.

explain: 길 바로 옆을 가리키고, '길가'와 거의 비슷하게 써요. '길가'는 길의 가장자리 쪽을, '길옆'은 길 바로 옆 어딘가를 가리키는 느낌이에요. '길옆에 세우다, 길옆에 있다'처럼 위치를 말할 때 자주 써요.
explain_en: It points to the area right next to a road and is used much like '길가'. '길가' feels like the edge of the road, while '길옆' feels like somewhere right beside it. It is often used to describe location, as in '길옆에 세우다' and '길옆에 있다'.
